course_subtitle: Welcome, future coding hero! Embark on an exciting visual programming adventure with Tobi 🐻. Snap colorful blocks, build amazing games, and unlock cool medals! 🐻🎮🚀

stations.title: Station 1: Introduction to PicToBlox & Animal Racing
stations.desc: Learn how to navigate the PicToBlox workspace, drag color-coded puzzle blocks, and program your very first sprite race!
stations.story:
🐻 Hello, creative future coder!

I am your friend Tobi the Coding Bear 🐻!

Today we will build Station 1: Introduction to PicToBlox & Animal Racing! 🌟 Slide to learn!

🎯 Slide 1: New Things to Learn!

✨ PicToBlox Workspace Layout: Exploring the Stage (preview), Blocks Palette (drawers), and Script Area (workspace).
✨ Dragging & Snapping Blocks: Combining blocks vertically like Lego blocks to build sequences.
✨ Stage Coordinate System: Moving sprites along horizontal X and vertical Y grid axes.

⛳ Slide 2: Our Goals Today!

🚀 Position the racing sprites on the left boundary using coordinate blocks.
🚀 Make your favorite animal sprite glide smoothly to the finish line.

🏆 Slide 3: The Mission!

Animal Racing Game: Program a rabbit and a turtle sprite to compete in a race to the finish line, playing cheering sounds when they cross!

🧩 Slide 4: Magic Puzzle Blocks!

go to x: 0 y: 0
glide 1 secs to x: 100 y: 50
say Let's race! for 2 seconds
start sound cheering ▾

Snap these blocks! When your game runs, click the Green Medal Button! 🏅
stations.simple: Imagine PicToBlox blocks are like Lego blocks! You snap one block on top of another to build a towering command that tells your sprite exactly where to go!
stations.hint: Click the big green button below: Done! Claim My Medal! once you build the race game in PicToBlox!
stations.challenge: Build your Animal Racing game in PicToBlox and click the green medal button below!

stations.title: Station 12: If-Else Statements (Duck Hunter 2)
stations.desc: Finish your arcade game by writing two-way outcome branches, layout layer stacking, and ammunition counts.
stations.story:
🐻 Hello, creative future coder!

I am your friend Tobi the Coding Bear 🐻!

Today we will build Station 12: If-Else Statements (Duck Hunter 2)! 🌟 Slide to learn!

🎯 Slide 1: New Things to Learn!

✨ Two-Way Decisions (If-Else): Executing code path A if true, or path B if false.
✨ Layer Stacking: Positioning sprites in front of or behind other graphical layers.
✨ Final Publishing: Polishing UI stats, score boundaries, and sounds.

⛳ Slide 2: Our Goals Today!

🚀 Use If-Else blocks to show 'You Win' or 'Game Over' screens.
🚀 Stack the targeting crosshair above all flying duck layers.

🏆 Slide 3: The Mission!

Duck Hunter Game (Part 2): Add ammunition counts, reload warnings, and layer stack order so the aiming sight is always in front. Display a Win screen if score exceeds 10, else a Game Over screen!

Snap these blocks! When your game runs, click the Green Medal Button! 🏅
stations.simple: An If-Else block is like a path split in a fairy tale! If you have the key, you open the castle gates. Else, you must take the detour path!
